cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's Audit Machine as it reviews events after the year end at HANGS Construction Services.
Subsequent events happen after the year end. It reads the minutes and the lawyers' letter.
Then it reads every receipt and payment after the year end.
Two June costs were paid later; one customer paid nothing.
Next it sorts the events: books or notes, depending on when the cause arose.
Then the going-concern test: can the company keep paying its bills for the next year?
Even after its adjustments, June 30 net worth clears the bank's minimum by about $379,000.
Without the bank's renewal of the credit line, the cash would run out.
Now it adds up what it found and sets it against materiality.
Then it writes the workpapers and a draft findings memo for the CPA.

All done. This review adds about $118,000 of adjustments, under materiality. The bigger issue is the notes: they leave out most later events and misstate the going-concern finding. Eleven items stay open. The CPA, a person, decides each one and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
